description: PROVISIONAL until RED lane lands the named test files. E16-7 portal SC-1 through SC-31; SC-23 is a recorded operator restore drill. Start PostgreSQL with `make -C apps/prototype-description-service postgres-start`. The repository-root command writes JUnit under .task-state/evals, then check_eval_junit.py fails the gate when failures+errors exceed max_failures 0 or skipped exceed max_skipped 0 and appends one JSONL evidence row.
command: mkdir -p .task-state/evals && (cd apps/prototype-description-service && ACX_PORTAL_TESTS_REQUIRE_PG=1 python3 -m pytest recognition/tests/api/test_portal_auth.py recognition/tests/api/test_portal_keys.py recognition/tests/api/test_portal_ui.py recognition/tests/infra/test_caddyfile_admin_404.py recognition/tests/api/test_admin_router.py recognition/tests/schema/test_identity_schema_pg.py recognition/tests/test_tenant_bound_api_key_repository.py recognition/tests/scripts/test_check_eval_junit.py -q -rs --junitxml=../../.task-state/evals/e16-7-portal.xml); python3 apps/prototype-description-service/scripts/check_eval_junit.py .task-state/evals/e16-7-portal.xml --suite e16-7-tenant-selfserve-key-panel --max-failures 0 --max-skipped 0 --append-jsonl .task-state/evals/results.jsonl

cases.criterion: Cross-tenant key access through the portal returns 404 or 403 and never exposes the other tenant's key.

An authenticated tenant sees full key history for the server-resolved tenant, including revoked rows with `revoked_at` set, plus `id`, `created_at`, `last_used_at`, and `expires_at`. Reads go through `TenantBoundApiKeyRepository` constructed with the server-resolved `tenant_id` (no caller-supplied tenant id; wraps `SqlAlchemyApiKeyRepository`) with `include_revoked=True`; a client-supplied tenant id cannot change the resolved tenant.

Equal idempotency key and fingerprint mint one replacement with the old rate tier and a fresh lifetime derived from the original lifetime; replay returns metadata without a secret, and a different fingerprint returns 422. Handlers build a frozen `PortalMutationContext(tenant_id, idempotency_key, request_fingerprint, clerk_sub, email, sid)` plus `key_id`; the service owns the reservation insert, key mutation, and audit row with `{clerk_sub, email, sid}`.

Rotation authorizes only an active key owned by the resolved tenant (404 foreign; 409 revoked, expired, or already rotated), keeps the old key active until the earlier original expiry or seven-day cutoff, and recognition classifies it expired afterward.
The raw key is shown exactly once in the first successful rotate response, is not re-shown on an idempotent replay, and never appears in application logs, audit rows, or URLs.
Every `/admin*` request on the `app.altcontext.com` vhost returns 404.
When Clerk JWKS is unreachable, the portal returns a distinct 503 while `/analyze` with a valid key still succeeds.

Concurrent equal rotate requests produce one new key and one old-key cutoff; the loser replays under re-applied tenant context. Distinct idempotency keys against the same old key yield one winner and a 409 loser.
Cross-tenant test: tenant B cannot read or replay tenant A's `portal_rotations` row, at both repository and RLS level.
A portal request carrying `X-Tenant-ID` for another tenant is served strictly as the Clerk-resolved tenant; the header is ignored (test asserts no cross-tenant rows returned).

Direct `POST /portal/keys/{id}/revoke` uses one conditional `UPDATE api_keys SET revoked_at=now() WHERE id=:id AND tenant_id=:tenant AND revoked_at IS NULL RETURNING id`. A returned row yields 200 with `revoked_at` set and one `audit_events` row in the same transaction; zero rows re-read to 404 (foreign/missing) or 409 (already revoked) with no audit row. Handlers build `PortalMutationContext` plus `key_id`; the service owns the transaction. `/portal` maps `already_revoked` to 409 and `UnknownKeyError`/foreign key to 404.

`GET /portal/me` returns exactly `{tenant_id, email, key_count}` for an eligible user and 403 `tenant_not_eligible` for an unmatched one, with a `portal_auth_events` row. The Clerk subject is not returned.
Missing `email` claim → 403 `claim_missing` with a `portal_auth_events` row whose `email_hash IS NULL`; `email_verified=false` → 403 `email_unverified` with a hashed email in its row.
The server-rendered page (`GET /portal/`) returns 200 HTML listing the tenant's keys with no `jinja2` in `sys.modules`.
If the `audit_events` insert fails inside rotate, the key mutation rolls back and no `portal_rotations` row survives.

Unauthenticated `GET /portal/` redirects (302) to Clerk sign-in; unauthenticated `GET /portal/keys` returns 401 `invalid_session`; a valid `__session` cookie and a valid bearer token each authenticate identically when presented alone.
A cross-site form POST to rotate/revoke with a valid `__session` cookie but missing/mismatched CSRF token or foreign Origin is rejected 403 `csrf_failed` and no key changes.
Tokens with bad signature, wrong `iss`, wrong `azp`, disallowed `alg`, expired `exp`, or future `nbf` each return 401 `invalid_session` and write no `portal_auth_events` row.
Each 403 (`tenant_not_eligible`, `email_unverified`, `claim_missing`) leaves exactly one committed `portal_auth_events` row observable from a fresh connection after the response.

Start PostgreSQL with `make -C apps/prototype-description-service postgres-start` before the eval command. With `ACX_PORTAL_TESTS_REQUIRE_PG=1` and PostgreSQL stopped, the portal DB tests FAIL (not skip).

A verified contact claims an unbound tenant once; later sessions resolve by unique issuer and subject after an email change, while a competing subject receives 403 and concurrent claims cannot create two bindings.

A lost first rotation response cannot reveal the secret on replay; the tenant can rotate the replacement with a new idempotency key, and a constant-provisioned install sees deployment guidance and cutoff.

Injected `portal_auth_events` insert failure still returns the intended 403 reason, logs ERROR without email/token material, and does not reuse the request session. The insert uses its own short-lived session, never the request session.

A request carrying both a `__session` cookie and an `Authorization: Bearer` header is rejected 401 `invalid_session` before any token is verified, regardless of either credential's validity, and writes no `portal_auth_events` row. Covers both-valid-different-principals and valid-cookie plus invalid-bearer.
Two concurrent direct revokes of one active key yield exactly one 200 and one 409, and exactly one audit row.

`/admin` revoke of an already-revoked key still returns 200 `already_revoked=true` with no second audit row after `recognition/interface_adapters/http/routers/admin.py::revoke_key_atomic` and `RevokeOutcome(record, already_revoked)` are extracted into a tenant-aware service. `UnknownKeyError` stays the not-found signal.

Inserting a `portal_auth_events` row with an unsupported `outcome` and non-NULL `email_hash` fails the CHECK. `portal_auth_events.outcome` has its own CHECK `outcome IN ('tenant_not_eligible','email_unverified','claim_missing')`, separate from the existing NULL/hash CHECK, in `001_identity_schema.py`.

`apps/prototype-description-service/api/main.py::create_app` registers `/portal/*` routes, and app construction raises when `ACX_CLERK_ISSUER`, `ACX_CLERK_JWKS_URL`, `ACX_CLERK_AUTHORIZED_PARTIES`, or `ACX_PORTAL_CSRF_SECRET` is missing.

`TenantBoundApiKeyRepository` bound to tenant A never returns tenant B rows for list/get/revoke, exercised without HTTP. The repository is constructed with the server-resolved `tenant_id` and exposes no method that accepts a caller-supplied tenant id; it wraps `SqlAlchemyApiKeyRepository`. Isolation is proven at repository level because `api_keys` is RLS-exempt.

`apps/prototype-description-service/scripts/check_eval_junit.py` exits non-zero for a JUnit file with one skipped case and zero failures, and zero for a clean file. It exits non-zero when failures+errors exceed max-failures or skipped exceed max-skipped, and appends one JSONL evidence row.
